newsitem.title: USA: US Justice settles United Tech military aid case.
newsitem.headline: US Justice settles United Tech military aid case.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday that United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney Group will pay $14.8 million for allegedly conspiring to help divert U.S. military aid into a slush fund controlled by a former Israeli Air Force officer.
It said the civil settlement resolved a lawsuit filed in federal court in Miami against the defense contractor.

The lawsuit had alleged that United Technologies and former Israeli Air Force officer Rami Dotan set up a $10 million fund with U.S. military aid. Dotan was sentenced in 1991 by an Israeli military court to 13 years in prison.
Assistant Attorney General Frank Hunger, head of the Justice Department's Civil Division, praised Israeli authorities for their help in investigating the case.

The lawsuit had alleged that United Technologies acquired the $10 million in funds for Dotan through false billings in 1987 under a contract with Israel for Pratt & Whitney engines for an Israeli fighter aircraft.
According to the lawsuit, the company and Dotan concealed a "side-deal" to use the money as a "bank" for Dotan, avoiding the required oversight by the Pentagon and by Israeli procurement authorities.
The Justice Department said General Electric Co previously pleaded guilty and paid civil damages and penalties in connection with a similar scheme carried out by Dotan.
